structure:
[part 1] Massachusetts History and Social Science Curriculum Framework 2018 (Pre-K-12). Front matter (cover, credits, vision, 10 Guiding Principles, scope and sequence, organization, how-to-read page) is backup; 'Standards for History and Social Science Practice, Pre-K-12' (7 practices) are standards PK-12 and are repeated as a sidebar list on each grade's introductory page. Each grade or course (Pre-K to Grade 8, then HS United States History I) has: (1) an introductory page with title, narrative, a topics list, literacy note and 'Looking Back, Looking Ahead' (title = standards, narrative/topics/looking back = examples), then (2) '<Grade> Content Standards' organised by numbered Topics with codes like [PreK.T1], [K.T2], [4.T4a], [6.T3b], [8.T5], [USI.T1] and a 'Supporting Question' (examples, unless in the same unit as a topic heading); numbered standards with a. b. c. sub-items, 'For example' text and 'Clarification Statement' (examples), 'Key/Suggested Primary Sources ... in Appendix D' (examples), and numbered footnotes (content footnotes = examples; footnotes in front matter, literacy and practice-statement notes = backup); then (3) 'History and Social Science and the Standards for Literacy' with grade-specific Reading Informational Text [RI], Writing [W], Speaking and Listening [SL] standards (Pre-K-5) or grades 6-8 [RCA-H, WCA, SLCA] literacy standards (backup). Grades 6-7 are a two-year world geography sequence labelled Grade 6 and Grade 7; Grade 8 is Civics (Topics 1-7). High school courses are titled 'United States History I' etc.; course = 'United States History I' for that course's own units, and the Practice standards sidebar is course null grades PK-12. The view is single-column text; tables are rare (a one-column 'Suggested sources' table in Grade 6). This part covers Pre-K through US History I Topic 7 up to u1192 (u1195 onward is labeled by another agent).
[part 2] Massachusetts History and Social Science Curriculum Framework (2018), part 2 of the file (u1195 onward): end of High School United States History I (Topic 7), then High School courses and electives each with an intro page (title, overview narrative with guiding questions, a boxed 'Standards for History and Social Science Practice, Pre-K-12' list that is split into several units, topic list, literacy note and 'connections' paragraph) followed by 'Content Standards' pages. Content standards are organized by Topic (codes such as [USII.T1], [WHI.T3], [GOV]/[T1]), each topic opens with a 'Supporting Question', then numbered standards 1..n with lettered sub-lists (a, b, c...), 'Clarification Statement' blocks, and 'Key/Suggested Primary Sources for Topic n in Appendix D' blocks; footnotes appear at page bottoms. Courses in range: United States History I (tail), United States History II, World History I, World History II, elective United States Government and Politics, elective Economics, Personal Financial Literacy, News/Media Literacy (HS stand-alone standard sets). Then Grades 9-10 and 11-12 Literacy Standards in the Content Areas (RCA-H, WCA, SLCA), Appendices A (English learners / students with disabilities), B (inquiry), C (using primary sources), and Appendix D (annotated primary source tables: column 1 source and annotation, last column the grade(s)/course(s) it is tied to; the World History table also has period header rows), ending with a note about the companion Resources document. All high school content is labeled grades 9-12 with the course name as written.
